annotationRationale: The identical AMC 10A question supplies a reviewed method, retained with both original reference credits. The main work compares winning probabilities conditional on the observed roll, then counts disjoint cases. The supplied variants use the same strategy and do not provide a genuinely different useful alternative.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Counting & Probability is the correct area. No repair is needed.

review.questionCheck: Under the usual independent fair-dice model, exactly two rerolls are strictly optimal precisely when the sorted initial roll satisfies \(a\leq3\) and \(a+b\geq7\). These conditions give 42 of 216 ordered rolls, or 7/36, choice A. No tie-breaking ambiguity affects the answer, and no figure conflict is present.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: 2020_AMC_10A_Q25 / compare-reroll-options is retained for the identical statement, choices and key. Its full argument independently verifies the result here. The supplied LIVE and AoPS variants use the same option comparison and smallest-face classification, so no additional genuinely different route is needed.
review.annotationCheck: Classical probability and probabilities conditional on the observed roll are appropriately assessed. Combined counting supports the final disjoint cases. Removing the table/tree procedure is reasonable because the table summarizes derived counts rather than enumerating a two-step sample space.
review.areaCheck: Counting & Probability is the correct area. No repair is needed.

methodReviews.mathCheck: Keeping k gives \((6-k)/36\), while rerolling all gives \(15/216=5/72\). An existing total of 7 makes zero rerolls optimal; otherwise a pair sum at most 6 permits a one-die success probability of 1/6, exceeding both alternatives. When every pair sums to at least 7, two rerolls beat three exactly for \(a\leq3\), with no equality case. The unique-smallest-die counts are 3, 12 and 27, giving 7/36.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: The exact shared question/method is credited, and both inherited reference IDs, live-reference-2020_AMC_10A_Q25 and aops-reference-2020_AMC_10A_Q25, are preserved. Current-question references are also supplied. The project reuse is accurately labeled source-informed-original, without claiming official MAA provenance.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: All four reroll sizes are compared, the optimal kept die is justified, and boundary and tie cases are settled. The supported table explains its entries through the unique minimum and independent choices for the other dice, establishing exhaustive counting without duplication.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: cnm_h244 matches the winning probabilities given each observed roll; cnm_h137 matches equally likely outcome counts; cnm_h232 matches disjoint cases and products. No unnecessary optimization theorem or conditional-probability machinery is assumed.
